newsitem.title: UK: NZ SPORT-England make front page, for wrong reason.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT-England make front page, for wrong reason.

text.p: LONDON, Feb 18 - England wrapped up their first overseas test cricket victory in five years in Christchurch last night, but their cricketers made the front pages at home for the wrong reason, NZPA reported on Wednesday (NZT).
While the cricket victory by four wickets was being celebrated on the back pages, the Evening Standard devoted its front page to the allegations surrounding England bowler Phil Tufnell.
He was also fined Stg800 ($NZ1887) in court for locking the mother of his child in a cupboard during a row over the break-up of their home, the Standard said.
Meanwhile, England captain Mike Atherton was being hailed as England's match-winner.
"Atherton's finest hour" said the Standard in its back page headline, rather unfortunately placed above an advertisement for male impotence.
Correspondent David Lloyd wrote: "England tasted sweet success here today with a victory which Mike Atherton will savour for years to come."
He added that Atherton's "Herculean" efforts deserved "more than a simple man-of-the-match award".

Dominic Cork and John Crawley may have seen England home with an unbeaten 76-run seventh wicket partnership, but "they and everyone else present at Lancaster Park would agree instantly that Atherton was the man who made everything possible," Lloyd wrote.
"He was on the field for all but three hours of this gripping contest, adding 118 to his first innings 94 not out.
"The only pity was that he did not manage to see his self-assigned job right the way through."
Lloyd said that Atherton had probably saved his job as captain for the home Ashes series against Australia later this year.
